recognize_zh: 這顆帶狀核（band）嗜中性球的細胞質充滿粗大、深紫藍色的顆粒，比正常嗜中性球的淡粉紅細小顆粒明顯粗且深，是毒性顆粒（toxic granulation）的表現。
features: Band neutrophil with a curved, non-segmented, C/U-shaped nucleus of uniform width
Cytoplasm packed with coarse, dark purple-blue (azurophilic) granules, much larger and darker than normal neutrophilic granules
Granules evenly distributed throughout the cytoplasm and do not obscure the nucleus
No clear cytoplasmic vacuoles or Döhle bodies identified in this cell
Surrounding red cells are normocytic and normochromic
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, high power, shows a band neutrophil with a horseshoe-shaped nucleus and condensed chromatin. The cytoplasm contains abundant coarse, dark azurophilic granules distributed evenly throughout, consistent with toxic granulation. Cytoplasmic vacuolization and Döhle bodies are not evident in this cell, and the background red cells are unremarkable. Findings are consistent with toxic granulation in a band neutrophil, as seen in infection, inflammation, or G-CSF therapy.

ddx.vs: Alder-Reilly granules are large, dark, and present in all leukocytes including lymphocytes and monocytes, and occur without clinical infection (mucopolysaccharidoses).
Chédiak-Higashi shows few giant, discrete, irregular granules rather than numerous uniform coarse granules.
Basophil granules are larger, blue-black, water-soluble, and typically overlie and obscure the nucleus.
Immature precursors have a round or oval nucleus with finer chromatin and often a paranuclear hof, rather than a mature condensed band nucleus.
